highlights.title: The blind spot
commentary: Axelrod Acolytes changed its move in 90% of rounds: defect, cooperate, defect, cooperate.
Two Strikes only answers two defections in a row, so alternating costs almost nothing.

highlights.title: The moment it gave up
commentary: Majority Rule cooperates while the opponent has cooperated more often than not.
Pavlov's defections crossed half the record at round 80. It never cooperated again.

highlights.title: One flip, and that was that
commentary: A single move flipped by noise in round 2 broke cooperation.
235 rounds later they were still defecting: neither could tell noise from intent.

highlights.title: Farming the forgiver
commentary: Pavlov switches after a loss, so it offers cooperation again every other round.
Always-defect took 3.06 a round from it; Pavlov's Dogs got 0.57.

highlights.title: The noisiest match
commentary: Forty-nine moves flipped by noise, more than any other match.
They still finished cooperating: both forgive faster than the noise breaks them.

highlights.title: Noise, absorbed
commentary: Eighteen flipped moves, and they still finished level at 2.96 apiece.
Being slow to take offence costs less than being quick to.

highlights.title: The champion's worst hour
commentary: The champion's lowest score of the tournament: 0.99 a round.
Against a bot that only ever defects, there is nothing better to do.

highlights.title: The title fight
commentary: First and second place met a hundred times; this is one of them.
Across everyone else they were level, so their own matches decided the tournament.
